background.text: Where do you see this going over the next two weeks or two months? Will this violence stop and downtown open up again?

ground_truth: Well, look, if I was great at predicting exactly how this would unfold, I would have predicted something very different than where we are today. Who would have predicted six months ago we'd be in a global pandemic, a global recession bordering on depression, civil unrest all across the United States? Nobody could have predicted this. So I'm officially, I'm out of the prediction business. But here's what I think is going to happen. Number one, calmer voices are going to prevail that the highly emotional, charged moment that we're in today, I hope that will subside. I hope the divisions we see in the community, people will start putting their passion and their divisions towards working together on meaningful common sense reform based on data, fact, and true information so that we can actually make some smart decisions. The council's already made a number of reforms, including moving the equity office in the police bureau under the police chief. We've supported, again, legislation at the state level that has passed. We've disbanded some specialty units that have disproportionately impacted people of color. But the hard work lies ahead. And the hard work is about reimagining what public safety looks like, reimagining what basic patrol services look like, and reforming this antiquated Byzantine oversight and accountability mechanism has really hobbled both the police bureau and the public at large for generations. I think there's a lot of hard work for all of us, but we've got to stop the back and the forth, the divisiveness, the politicization of this issue, and really start focusing on the facts and what it's going to take to provide a smart, strong, effective, well-resourced police bureau that has everybody's safety interests at mind. That's what really the goal is here.
